done_when: A task's review reads the story doc (its row, Done-when items and details) from the same place forge task start does: the story branch's copy while the story branch exists, else the default branch's. A command-level test edits a task's row on the story branch after approval and shows the review prompt carries the edited row.

findings.body: After one review, commit another task-row or details edit only on the story branch and run `forge close` again without changing task code. `fingerprint()` still hashes the task commit's plan (`src/forge/review.py:145`), while the prompt now reads the story branch's plan. Consequently, `src/forge/close.py:79–87` considers the previous review fresh and skips reviewing the edited contract. This can preserve blocking findings for work moved to another task, or reuse a clean review against outdated requirements. Include the selected story-document content in the freshness calculation so changes to the actual review input invalidate the cached result.
findings.title: Fingerprint the story document used by the review

why: A task's review reads the story doc from the default branch while forge next and forge task start read it from the story branch, so a plan edit made in the story worktree after approval never reaches the reviewer and the review raises findings for work the plan moved to another task
